issues.legal_issue: A consumer complaint filed more than two years after its cause of action arose is barred unless sufficient cause for the delay is shown.
material_facts: The alleged shortfall in the allotted area was discovered when possession was received in January 1987.
The alleged harm from the neighbouring shop’s bhatties began before 1989 and ceased when they were removed in 1994.
The consumer complaint was filed in 1997, and it contained no request to condone the delay or explanation establishing sufficient cause.
issues.conclusion: The complaint was barred by limitation, which was sufficient to allow the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24-A of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 requires a consumer forum to dismiss a complaint filed more than two years after the cause of action arose unless the complainant satisfies the forum that sufficient cause prevented timely filing. The State Commission and National Commission had not considered the limitation objection.

rule.if: consumer_complaint and cause_of_action_over_two_years_earlier and not sufficient_cause_for_delay_shown

predicates.consumer_complaint: A person filed a complaint before a consumer forum alleging a deficiency in service.
predicates.cause_of_action_over_two_years_earlier: The complaint was filed more than two years after the events giving rise to the alleged cause of action.
predicates.sufficient_cause_for_delay_shown: The complainant established to the forum a sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within the prescribed period.

issues.definition: When a consumer complaint is filed more than two years after its cause of action arose and the complainant has not shown sufficient cause for delay, the complaint is barred by limitation.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation award cannot stand when its factual premise is contradicted by the record and the record provides no basis for the award.
material_facts: The National Commission awarded compensation on the basis that the bhatties had been removed during the appeal before it and that their presence had caused hardship and health hazards.
The complaint itself stated that the bhatties had been removed in 1994, three years before the complaint was filed.
The Court found no basis in the circumstances for the compensation award.
issues.conclusion: The compensation award was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found that the National Commission relied on a factual premise contrary to the record and that there was no basis for awarding compensation. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_against_consumer_compensation_awa: A party appealed an order of a consumer forum awarding compensation.
predicates.award_based_on_fact_contradicted_by_reco: The consumer forum relied on a factual premise that the record showed to be incorrect.
predicates.no_basis_for_compensation_award: The record and circumstances supplied no basis for the compensation awarded.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a consumer compensation award, the award rests on a factual premise contradicted by the record, and there is no basis for the award, the award is set aside.
